contests.title: Thorp School District — School facility improvement borrowing

provenance.quote: Replacing and/or repairing school roof, HVAC system, asphalt, electrical systems, plumbing systems, fire safety equipment, worn out windows, lockers, bleachers, exterior repairs.

contests.title: Unity School District — Question I — School facility borrowing

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the Unity School District, Polk County,
Wisconsin that there shall be issued pursuant to Chapter 67 of the Wisconsin Statutes, general
obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $32,000,000 for the public purpose of paying the
cost of a school facility improvement project at the district campus consisting of: construction of
an addition and renovations at the High School, including for career and technical education and
automotive space, and cafeteria and food service updates; safety, traffic flow, parking and site
improvements; district-wide capital maintenance and building infrastructure improvements,
including roof replacement; athletic facility and accessibility improvements, and reconstruction
of baseball, football and softball fields, the tennis courts and track; and acquisition of
furnishings, fixtures and equipment.

contests.title: Unity School District — Question II — Ongoing operating revenue-limit increase

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the Unity School District, Polk County,
Wisconsin that the revenues included in the School District budget be authorized to exceed the
revenue limit specified in Section 121.91, Wisconsin Statutes, by $600,000 beginning with the
2026-2027 school year, for recurring purposes consisting of operational and maintenance
expenses.

contests.title: Waunakee Community School District — Question 1 — Ongoing operating revenue-limit increases

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the Waunakee Community School District,
Dane County, Wisconsin that the revenues included in the School District budget be authorized
to exceed the revenue limit specified in Section 121.91, Wisconsin Statutes, by $4,200,000 for
the 2027-2028 school year; by an additional $2,100,000 for the 2028-2029 school year; by an
additional $2,100,000 for the 2029-2030 school year; and by an additional $2,100,000 for the
2030-2031 school year (for a total of $10,500,000 and to remain at that amount thereafter), for
recurring purposes consisting of ongoing operational expenses and employee compensation
expenses.

contests.title: Waunakee Community School District — Question 2 — School facility borrowing

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the Waunakee Community School District,
Dane County, Wisconsin that there shall be issued pursuant to Chapter 67 of the Wisconsin
Statutes, general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $97,500,000 for the public purpose
of paying the cost of a school facility improvement project consisting of: removal of an older
portion of the High School and construction of additions and renovations at the High School;
renovations at the old middle school (known as the High School South Campus); outdoor athletic
field renovations and improvements at the High School Campus; district-wide renovations,
capital maintenance and site improvements; and acquisition of furnishings, fixtures and
equipment.

provenance.quote: For non-recurring purposes consisting of operational expenses, including but not limited to school safety, staffing, and facility maintenance.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allow the district to borrow up to $8.5 million through general obligation bonds for district-wide capital maintenance and building infrastructure improvements, including plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling, roof, asphalt and fire-safety repairs and replacements, plus furnishings, fixtures and equipment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $8.5 million in borrowing for those school facility improvements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allow the district to borrow up to $32 million through general obligation bonds for high-school additions and renovations, including career and technical education, automotive, cafeteria and food-service spaces; safety, traffic, parking and site work; district-wide capital maintenance and infrastructure, including roof replacement; athletic and accessibility improvements and reconstruction of fields, tennis courts and track; and furnishings, fixtures and equipment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $32 million in borrowing for those district-campus improvements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Permanently raise the district’s annual state revenue limit by $600,000 beginning in the 2026–27 school year for operating and maintenance expenses.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the ongoing $600,000 yearly revenue-limit increase for operating and maintenance expenses.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Permanently raise the district’s annual state revenue limit by $4.2 million in 2027–28, then add $2.1 million in each of the next three school years. The total yearly increase would be $6.3 million in 2028–29, $8.4 million in 2029–30 and $10.5 million from 2030–31 onward, for ongoing operating and employee compensation expenses.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve those phased-in, ongoing revenue-limit increases, reaching $10.5 million a year from 2030–31 onward, for operating and employee compensation expenses.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allow the district to borrow up to $97.5 million through general obligation bonds to demolish an older High School portion and build additions and renovations; renovate the former middle school, now the High School South Campus; improve outdoor athletic fields at the High School Campus; make district-wide renovations, capital maintenance and site improvements; and buy furnishings, fixtures and equipment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $97.5 million in borrowing for those school facility improvements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allow the district to exceed its state revenue limit by $1.5 million a year for four school years, 2027–28 through 2030–31, for operating expenses, including school safety, staffing and facility maintenance. The increase would be temporary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the temporary $1.5 million yearly revenue-limit increase for those four years and operating purposes.
